name: Peng Zhihui
current_role: Co-founder, President and CTO, AgiBot (Zhiyuan Robotics), Shanghai
profile: Peng Zhihui (born 1993, Ji'an, Jiangxi), known online as 'Zhihui Jun' (稚晖君), is an engineer and Bilibili tech creator. After stints at Oppo's AI lab and Huawei's Ascend unit as a 'Genius Youth' hire, he left in Dec 2022 and co-founded humanoid-robot maker AgiBot with CEO Deng Taihua in Feb 2023; it is now one of China's largest humanoid makers.
interesting_fact: His homemade self-driving, self-balancing bicycle went viral on Bilibili in 2021; he has 2.5M+ followers there as 'Zhihui Jun'.
deep_cut_fact: He studied biomedical engineering at UESTC, and in 2021 built 'Dummy', an Iron Man-inspired desktop robotic arm that could thread a needle and stitch grape skins; a 2018 bipedal robot of his won an innovation award at the World Robot Olympiad.
notes: Very active public creator; Bilibili/GitHub are his own channels. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: George Bevis
current_role: CEO of Scram (software startup); founder of Tide (stepped down as Tide CEO in 2018)
profile: British serial entrepreneur who founded Tide, the UK SME business-banking app, in 2015 after a career at Capital One, Barclaycard, Zopa, WorldPay and RBS. Tide now serves 1.5M+ small businesses. He handed the CEO role to Oliver Prill in 2018 and now runs Scram, aiming to change how serious organisations build software.
interesting_fact: An earlier start-up, Speedsell (reselling second-hand goods for a catalogue retailer), wound up and left him broke; he says that experience led to Tide.
deep_cut_fact: He founded Crucible, an initiative preparing talented teenagers to help build prosperity in Africa, and CanDo, a social-ventures incubator; in 2012 he wrote a book on small-business policy for a political party.

public_contacts.value: press@tide.co (Tide press team; he is no longer CEO)
https://www.founderspledge.com/contact-form (Founders Pledge, where he is listed as a member)

notes: No personal channels verified. 'Scram' website not confirmed (not the SCRAM Systems alcohol-monitoring firm). Founders Pledge member profile suggests philanthropy angle.

name: Wan Jun
current_role: Founder, Chairman, Executive Director and CEO, DeepWay (深向科技), Beijing
profile: Wan Jun (万钧, b. 1972, Chongqing) studied economics at Renmin University and was assistant president/VP at Zoomlion (2007-12), then founded commercial-vehicle finance group Lionbridge (狮桥) in 2012. In 2020 he co-founded electric heavy-truck maker DeepWay with Baidu, licensing Baidu Apollo autonomy; it filed for a Hong Kong IPO in Nov 2025.
interesting_fact: DeepWay was billed as China's first 'new force' heavy-truck startup and holds Baidu Apollo's only 'white-box' autonomous-driving licence for commercial vehicles.
deep_cut_fact: Before founding Lionbridge he ran Zoomlion's financial-leasing subsidiary; he is also a council member of the China EV100 forum and vice chair of the Tianjin Federation of Industry and Commerce.
notes: No verified public contact found; route via DeepWay corporate/IR after HK listing. Chinese-language outreach advisable.

name: Jia Peng
current_role: Co-founder and CEO, Simplexity Robotics (至简动力)
profile: Jia Peng (贾鹏) is a former NVIDIA senior architect who led autonomous-driving R&D at Li Auto. He left in 2025 and co-founded embodied-AI startup Simplexity Robotics with ex-Li Auto colleagues Wang Kai and Wang Jiajia; it raised ~RMB 2B in five rounds in six months (backers incl. Tencent, Alibaba, HongShan), hitting a $1B+ valuation.
interesting_fact: Simplexity became the fastest unicorn in China's embodied-AI sector, about seven months after founding.
deep_cut_fact: At NVIDIA GTC 2025 he gave a keynote unveiling Li Auto's next-generation 'MindVLA' vision-language-action driving architecture.
notes: Low public profile; no verified contact. Company has presence in Beijing, Shanghai, Suzhou.
